uncited: This family covers techniques for rendering specular highlights, mirror-like reflections, and iridescent effects in distance-field ray marching.
It solves the problem of simulating view-dependent surface reflectance in implicit geometry, where standard rasterization techniques are not directly applicable.

It sets itself apart from [Distance Color Blending](791-distance-color-blending.md) by handling geometric specular bounces rather than volumetric color blending, and from [Diffuse Lighting Models](5343-diffuse-lighting-models.md) by explicitly modeling view-dependent reflectance [S1, unofficial][S2].
The concept of ray marching for implicit surfaces was popularized by Inigo Quilez [S1, unofficial].
Spherical Gaussians for lighting approximation were introduced by Schlick [S1, unofficial][S2].
The specific neon shading model is derived from real-time procedural city rendering techniques [S1, unofficial].
